content.text:
**Finding submitted: MISSING (critical) — no Vendor indemnity exists.**

What I found:

- **Section 7 is a false friend.** Its heading reads "LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR," but the three subparagraphs contain only a mutual cap at fees paid (7(a)), a consequential-damages waiver (7(b)), and a mutual attorneys'-fees waiver (7(c)). A full-text search for "indemn" across the document returns **only the heading** — there is no operative indemnity in either direction.
- **The IP warranty doesn't fill the gap.** Section 5(c) warrants that the Works and third-party products don't infringe, but a warranty carries no duty to defend. Worse, a breach-of-warranty claim would be capped at fees paid under 7(a), and 7(c) makes us eat our own defence costs — so a third-party patent suit over RadialSpark's deliverables would land almost entirely on us. Per the detection guidance, this fails even the fallback (no Vendor IP indemnity at all = walk-away territory).
- **Drafting error worth flagging in negotiation:** 7(a)'s carve-out from the cap points to "Contractor's obligations pursuant to Paragraph 9," but Paragraph 9 is Independent Contractor status. This strongly suggests an indemnity section was dropped during drafting — useful leverage for framing our insert as a restoration rather than a new ask.
- **Nothing to narrow on our side.** Because no Customer indemnity exists, the second half of the rule (keep Customer's indemnity narrow) needed no edit — and I did not manufacture one.

The redline (validated `ok:true`) inserts the preferred four-prong Contractor indemnity as new 7(d) with notice/control/cooperation mechanics, expressly carved out of 7(a)–(c) so the cap and fee waiver can't hollow it out, and conforms the misleading heading to "INDEMNIFICATION." The comment offers the 3× annual fees super-cap as a fallback if RadialSpark resists uncapped exposure.

One item outside this rule's scope that the deal team may want to route to the appropriate playbook rule: the 7(a) cap at "fees paid" is low, and the mutual attorneys'-fees waiver in 7(c) is unusual and cuts against us in any enforcement action. I did not flag those here to avoid double-counting the same commercial term under two rules.
